# Miqsat Ma'ase Ha-Torah Section 6 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** 4QMMT (4Q394–399, Cave 4), Section C | **Condition:** Fragmentary; reconstructed from multiple manuscripts

---

**6:1** And you know that no treachery or deceit or evil is found in our hand, since for [these matters] we give [...]

**6:2** [...] And indeed we have written to you [...] for your good and for the good of your people [...]

**6:3** [...] for we saw that you have wisdom and knowledge of the Torah. Consider [...]

**6:4** [...] all the things that have come upon you [...] and you will find [...]

**6:5** [And in]deed we have [written] to you some of the works of the Torah which we believe are good for you and for your people, for we saw that you have wisdom and knowledge of the Torah.

**6:6** Consider all these things and ask Him to direct your counsel aright and to keep far from you evil scheming and the counsel of Belial,

**6:7** so that you may rejoice at the end of time, when you find that some of our words are true.

**6:8** And it shall be reckoned to you as righteousness, when you do what is right and good before Him, for your good and for the good of Israel.

**6:9** [...] for [...] in the Book of Moses it is written [...] and in the words of the Prophets [...]

**6:10** [...] that the blessings came [...] in the days of Solomon the son of David [...] and also the curses [...]

**6:11** [...] that came from the days of Jeroboam the son of Nebat until the exile of Jerusalem and Zedekiah king of Judah [...]

**6:12** [...] that He will bring upon them [...] and it is written [...] in the Book of Moses and in the [words of the] Prophets that [...]

**6:13** [...] [the bles]sings came in the days of David and Solomon [...] and the curses came from [...] until [...]

**6:14** [...] and we recognize that some of the blessings and the curses that are written in the Book of [Moses] have already come to pass [...]

**6:15** And this is the end of days, when they shall return in Israel for[ever ...] and shall not turn back [...]

**6:16** [...] but the wicked shall act [...] and [...] remember [...]

**6:17** Remember the kings of Israel and contemplate their deeds: whoever among them feared [the To]rah was delivered from troubles;

**6:18** those were the seekers of the Torah whose transgressions were forgiven.

**6:19** Remember David, who was a man of pious deeds, and he too was delivered from many troubles and was forgiven.

**6:20** And moreover we have written to you some of the works of the Torah [...] that it should be for your good [...]

**6:21** [...] for [...] you shall receive [...] at the end of time [...] when you walk in uprightness before Him [...]

**6:22** [...] and it shall be reckoned to you as righteousness [...] for doing what is upright and good before Him [...]

**6:23** [...] for your good and for the good of Israel [...]

**6:24** [...] and it is written: [...] at the end of days [...]

**6:25** [...] and remember all the words of Moses, the servant of God [...]

---

*SOPHIA notes: Section C is the theological summit of MMT and one of the most consequential passages in the Dead Sea Scrolls. The phrase "it shall be reckoned to you as righteousness" (6:8, 6:22) deliberately echoes Gen 15:6 and constitutes the earliest known link between "works of the Torah" and "reckoning as righteousness" — a connection that illuminates Paul's argument in Galatians 2–3 and Romans 3–4. SOPHIA retains EMET's "feared the Torah" (6:17) over LOGOS's "revered" because the Hebrew yare' fundamentally means "to fear" and carries that force here. "Pious deeds" (chasadim) connects to the project's broader treatment of chesed-vocabulary. "Seekers of the Torah" is a sectarian self-designation preserved literally. "Works of the Torah" is maintained as the title phrase. The eschatological framework — "end of days," "end of time" — situates the legal disputes within apocalyptic urgency.*
